intro: Temple texts are built from a small number of set phrases. Counts are from the published translations of the Hall’s interior wall reliefs (OIP 142), so they show what you will meet most often.

phrases.tells: Someone is talking. The name after it tells you who: usually a god speaking to the king.
phrases.where: In front of gods in ritual scenes; more than 100 times in the published wall texts.

phrases.meaning: The king has been given life by the gods.
phrases.tells: It follows the king’s names. Often extended: “given life like Re”.
phrases.where: After royal names everywhere; more than 300 times in the wall texts.

phrases.meaning: As the sun god is, forever.
phrases.tells: Ends many blessings: the king will live, rule or appear “like Re”, every day and forever.
phrases.where: The most common closing phrase: over 500 times in the wall texts.

phrases.meaning: A god’s promise to the king.
phrases.tells: What follows is the gift: life, dominion, millions of years, all lands under your sandals. The god gives because the king has served him.
phrases.where: In gods’ speeches; over 400 times in the wall texts.

phrases.meaning: The three gifts gods most often give.
phrases.tells: Look for the three signs in a row, often in a column of signs behind the king or in the god’s hand.
phrases.where: About 200 times in the wall texts.

phrases.meaning: Ruler of Upper and Lower Egypt.
phrases.tells: A title that comes just before a royal name.
phrases.where: About 300 times in the wall texts.

citations.locator: Frequency of “lord of the Two Lands”

phrases.meaning: Lord of crowns; the one who appears in glory.
phrases.tells: Usually stands before the birth name.
phrases.where: About 160 times in the wall texts.

phrases.meaning: A way of referring to the living king.
phrases.tells: Tells you the king is meant, not one of the gods in the scene.
phrases.where: Before royal names throughout the Hall.

phrases.text: King of Upper and Lower Egypt
phrases.meaning: Literally “he of the sedge and the bee”.
phrases.where: Before the first cartouche of every pair.

phrases.meaning: The king as the sun god’s son.
phrases.where: Before the second cartouche of every pair; see the painted beam.

phrases.meaning: Loved by Amun, the god of Karnak.
phrases.tells: Often part of a royal name itself (Ramesses-meryamun). The Amun group comes first out of respect.

phrases.meaning: A title of gods such as Amun-Re.
phrases.tells: Tells you the figure is a god.
phrases.where: About 140 times in the wall texts.

phrases.meaning: The opening of the king’s Horus name.
phrases.tells: You are reading the king’s Horus name, usually inside a palace-front frame (serekh).
phrases.where: About 60 times in the wall texts.

phrases.tells: Gods promise the king a reign without end.
phrases.where: In gods’ speeches and on year staves (scene B93, beside stop 6).

phrases.meaning: The festival that renewed the king.
phrases.tells: Gods promise “millions of jubilees”: many renewals of the king’s power.
phrases.where: On year staves and in speeches.

phrases.meaning: Justified: said of someone who has died and passed judgement.
phrases.tells: The person named is dead. Sety I is called “true of voice” at stop 6.
phrases.where: After names of deceased kings, such as Sety I in scene B92.
